# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Riley Lawson
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-24**
- **Member:** Riley Lawson
- **Member ID:** W287344319
- **Reference number:** POC-D304BE9399-97960
- **Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
- **Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## 1. What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), which Cigna issued on 2026-08-24 under reference number POC-D304BE9399-97960. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure my surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented as needed.

The notice states that the clinical records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. Respectfully, I believe the records already in Cigna's possession show otherwise when they are compared to the plan's own written criteria in Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026. Below I quote that policy and match each quoted requirement to what is in my chart.

## 2. The plan's criteria and the records, side by side

### The conservative care requirement — the reason given for the denial

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

My records document the following provider-directed non-surgical care:

- **Supervised physical therapy**, focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, from **2026-03-28 to 2026-07-04 — 14 weeks, 16 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **NSAIDs for 6 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-26**, which gave two weeks of partial relief.
- My symptoms have continued for **18 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest**, despite this care.

The policy also states:

> "an image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid) to which there was a positive response (i.e., any degree of pain reduction achieved within two (2) weeks after the injection)"

The plan's own wording sets the bar at "any degree of pain reduction achieved within two (2) weeks after the injection." My chart records a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-26 that produced partial relief lasting two weeks — a documented positive response, not a lack of one. So that my file is complete on this point, I ask that the injection procedure note be reviewed: [ask Dr. Duval's office to confirm from the 2026-04-26 procedure note whether the injection was image-guided and intra-articular, and to send that note with this appeal].

In short, the non-surgical treatment described in the passage quoted above is treatment I have already completed and documented, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

### Imaging

The policy states:

> "Imaging shows BOTH of the following findings:"

and

> "femoroacetabular impingement confirmed on x-ray, MRI, or CT with ANY of the following findings:"

with the listed findings including:

> "decrease of femoral head-neck offset"

> "acetabular retroversion (i.e., crossover sign, ischial spine sign)"

and

> "presence of Tönnis Grade 0-1 osteoarthritis"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip dated **2026-07-23** shows an **anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees**, with **joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0**. Femoroacetabular impingement is therefore confirmed on MRI, and Tonnis grade 0 falls within the "Tönnis Grade 0-1" range the policy names. I ask that the reviewing physician read the MRI arthrogram report itself and identify which of the listed imaging findings it satisfies, rather than treating the imaging criterion as unmet.

### Physical examination

The policy states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings:"

and names:

> "positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation)"

> "limited passive hip internal rotation"

My examination is documented as **positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain**. So the reviewer can match the exam findings to the exact language above, I ask that the office note be reviewed in full: [ask Dr. Duval's office to provide the examination note specifying the anterior impingement sign result and the measured passive hip internal rotation].

### Symptoms

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and that significantly limits activities"

My records describe **sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting**, and that I **cannot run or squat**. That is groin-dominant pain, worsened by flexion in the exact examples the policy gives — sitting and squatting — and it significantly limits my activities.

## 3. A note on the criteria themselves

Several of the passages I have quoted end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me. I am not able to quote those additional items, and I have not attempted to restate them. I ask that Cigna identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria in Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 that my request was found not to meet, and the specific records the reviewer relied on in reaching that conclusion. Apart from the passages quoted above, I have not been given the plan's language, and I have not assumed any threshold, duration or measurement that the plan has not published.

## 4. What I am asking Cigna to do

I respectfully ask Cigna to:

1. Overturn the 2026-08-24 denial and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914, as requested by Dr. Duval;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with expertise in orthopedic hip surgery;
3. If the denial is maintained, provide a written explanation identifying the exact criterion not met and the records reviewed, along with instructions for external review.

Documents submitted or available on request: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-28 to 2026-07-04, 16 visits), the MRI arthrogram report of 2026-07-23, the 2026-04-26 injection note, and Dr. Duval's office notes. [List any additional documents you are enclosing.]

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-20**. I am submitting it through my plan's appeal process at my.cigna.com, and I can be reached at 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my card with any questions; I am using the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Thank you for taking another look at this. I appreciate the time the reviewer gives to my file.

Sincerely,

**Riley Lawson**
Member ID: W287344319
